provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Int family batch. Mostly subcontractors with a homeowner repair side; copy splits between patch-and-texture homeowners, builders, and hiring hangers and tapers. Asbestos testing stays a referral, never a claim. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Orange peel, knockdown, skip trowel, hand-applied and smooth level-five finishes, with close-ups, and how a patch is feathered and matched so it disappears under paint
pageStructurePlus.why: Homeowners call because they're afraid the patch will show. A texture guide with close-ups proves the drywall finisher can make it vanish.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Testing the ceiling before scraping through a licensed lab [testing partner], plastic containment, scraping, skim coating smooth or retexturing, primer, and how long each room takes
pageStructurePlus.why: Popcorn removal is the most searched homeowner job in this trade, and the asbestos question decides whether people call at all.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Doorknob holes, water-stained and sagging ceilings, settling cracks over doors, nail pops, lifting tape, and a photo-based repair quote
pageStructurePlus.why: People search by the damage they're looking at. A page per damage type catches the search and sets the price expectation.

pageStructurePlus.section: Hang and finish for builders and GCs
pageStructurePlus.contains: Crew capacity in boards per week, levels of finish, fire-rated assemblies, insurance certificates on request, schedule reliability and a bid request for plans
pageStructurePlus.why: Most drywall revenue comes from builders and general contractors, who choose a sub on capacity, paperwork and showing up when framing is done.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Pay ranges, the path from helper to finisher to crew lead, tools provided, stilts and bench work, and a short apply form
pageStructurePlus.why: Drywall shops are limited by crew more than by demand. A real careers page brings applicants a feed post never will.

designDirections.name: Patch and Match
designDirections.bestFor: Small drywall outfits doing homeowner patches, water-damage repair and popcorn removal
designDirections.headlineSample: Drywall repair and texture matching in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: Denim and butter with geometric caps feel like a work order, and the page runs straight to the photo repair quote.

designDirections.name: Smooth Ceilings
designDirections.bestFor: Finishers with strong before-and-after ceilings, texture matches and smooth level-five walls to show
designDirections.headlineSample: Popcorn gone, ceilings smooth, walls patched in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo, Terracotta Kiln, fails the CTA contrast rule. Brick and Linen keeps the warm ground with a brick accent that passes, and the slab type suits a tradesman's portfolio.

designDirections.name: Board and Mud
designDirections.bestFor: Hang-and-finish subcontractors selling to builders and GCs, with a careers page that keeps crews full
designDirections.headlineSample: Hang, tape and finish crews for {City} builders
designDirections.whyItFits: A capability site fits the trade's real buyer, the builder. Steel blue and a plain grotesque read like a bid sheet, with capacity and insurance up front.

openers.line: Someone in {City} with a hole in the drywall searches, finds your listing, and has nothing to tap but a number. No texture close-ups, no idea if you do small patches.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's what a drywall repair customer would land on: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your listing goes to a Facebook page. A homeowner with a water-stained ceiling wants to see texture matches and send a photo, not scroll your posts.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link and confirm it lands on Facebook. Note the newest drywall job there.
openers.linkLine: A drywall page that takes a photo of the damage: {demo-link}

openers.line: The drywall site on your listing has a free-host banner and still says you're hiring from a post years old. Builders and homeowners both read that as a shop that's slowed down.
openers.hook: Open the site and look for banners, old dates or stale hiring notes. Note which.

openers.line: On my phone your site's popcorn ceiling photos are tiny thumbnails that don't open. That before-and-after is exactly what sells the job.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Drywall before-and-afters that open on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Most drywall patches can be roughly priced from one photo with a tape measure in the shot. There's no way to send you that except texting a stranger.
openers.hook: Check for any form. If quotes only happen by call or text, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A drywall repair form that takes a photo of the damage: {demo-link}

openers.angle: Texture work with nowhere to live
openers.line: That knockdown ceiling match you posted is invisible, which is the whole skill. A texture gallery would show homeowners you can make a patch disappear.
openers.hook: Find a texture-match or smooth-finish post. Name the texture if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your texture matches sorted by type: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews say nobody can find where the drywall patch was and the dust stayed in one room. That's the exact fear people have, and it's stuck on your listing.
openers.hook: Copy one review phrase about invisible patches or clean-up. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those reviews next to the drywall work: {demo-link}

openers.line: Winter is when people stuck indoors finally decide to get rid of the popcorn ceiling. The drywall finishers who show up in that search book their slow months.
openers.hook: Use this November to February. Mention winter in the reply.
openers.linkLine: A popcorn ceiling page ready for winter: {demo-link}

openers.line: A ceiling stain from an upstairs leak is found at night. If there's a way to send you a photo then, you're the first drywall call in the morning.
openers.hook: Call their listed number after hours. If voicemail only and no form, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A drywall damage request that works at night: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw the post looking for drywall hangers and tapers. Good finishers want to see pay, steady builder work and a real company before they switch crews.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note. Note the date and the role.
openers.linkLine: A drywall careers page for hangers and tapers: {demo-link}

openers.line: You hang and finish across {City}, but a homeowner in {Neighborhood} can't tell whether you'll come out for a single drywall patch there.
openers.hook: Find towns named in reviews or posts. Use the one furthest out.
openers.linkLine: A drywall page for each area you cover: {demo-link}

openers.line: Builders choosing a drywall sub look for capacity, insurance and a crew that shows up after framing inspection. A page saying that does your bidding before you call.
openers.hook: Look for builder tags or new-construction posts. If they have any, lead with this.

openers.line: People with popcorn ceilings in older homes worry about what's in them. A page explaining testing before any drywall scraping answers that before they ask.
openers.hook: Check whether they mention testing in posts. Never claim they test; say how it's handled.
openers.linkLine: Popcorn testing and removal explained on one drywall page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Looks like most of your drywall work comes through a couple of general contractors. That's steady until one slows down, and homeowner patch work fills the gap.
openers.hook: Look for posts tagging the same builder or GC repeatedly. Name them if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Where homeowner drywall work would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is flat, clean drywall finishing. Work that tidy should be the first thing a builder or homeowner sees.
openers.hook: Pick their newest posted job and name it by finish or texture.
openers.linkLine: That drywall job, front and centre: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner}, that {specific recent job} you posted is really clean drywall finishing.

I was looking for drywall contractors in {City} and found {Business Name}, but no site where a homeowner can send a photo of the damage or a builder can see your crew capacity. I put together a sample drywall site, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Want me to send it?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up in case this got buried. Here's the sample drywall site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a photo repair form, a texture-matching gallery, a popcorn ceiling page, a builder capability page and a careers page for hangers and tapers. If it's not for you, just say so.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for drywall companies here in {City}. I sent a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"No worries. Short version: I built a sample drywall site for {Business Name}, with a photo repair form for homeowners, a page for builders, and a careers page for tapers, plus marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I text the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range} depending on how many texture and area pages you want, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For a drywall shop your size I'd quote about {Build Price}."
"Is crew or work the bigger problem right now? The careers page and the builder page solve different ones."

CLOSE:
"I'll send a short scope and the deposit invoice, and we'll start with whichever page fixes your bigger problem."

objections.objection: I'm a sub, I don't need homeowners.
objections.handler: "Then the site is for builders and hires: capacity, insurance on request, and a careers page. Homeowner patches are optional filler for slow weeks."

objections.objection: My problem is crew, not work.
objections.handler: "That's why the careers page leads. Pay, path to finisher and a short apply form brings tapers a feed post never reaches."

objections.objection: Patch jobs are too small to bother with.
objections.handler: "Alone, yes. A photo form lets you price them in a minute and batch them on slow days. Popcorn ceilings and water damage aren't small."

objections.objection: I get work from a lead platform.
objections.handler: "Shared leads go to several drywall guys and you pay either way. Your own site sends that ceiling to one company, you."
"New builders and out-of-town GCs do, when their usual sub is booked. The capability page is how they find a second drywall crew."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}: a repair form, a texture gallery, a builder page and a careers page."

email.subject: Drywall site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "{Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for drywall companies in {City} and made a sample one for {Business Name}, including a careers page for tapers. I'll text you the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm pulling the {Business Name} drywall demo down on Friday.

Keep it up? One word is fine.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner}, popcorn ceiling season is starting as people head indoors for winter. Thought of you.

The drywall site is still ready, same price. {demo-link} for another look.

bullets: Ask first whether crew or work is the bottleneck, and lead the build with the careers page or the builder page to match.
Peg the build to a few homeowner patch jobs or a small slice of one builder contract, never to an hourly rate.
The photo repair form is the homeowner core. Price it inside the build; extra damage-type pages are cheap lines.
Price popcorn removal pages only for shops that handle containment and work with a testing partner.
Builder capability pages need real capacity and insurance details from the client. Leave bracketed placeholders until supplied.
Keep monthly add-ons small. Drywall shops run lean and won't pay for tools they don't use weekly.

lineItems.description: Max when the page has before-and-afters, a repair time estimate and an FAQ for that damage.
Max with several uploads, a size helper, a water-source question and text alerts to the owner.
Max with pay ranges, a role ladder, crew photos and a screening question set.

lineItems.item: Builder capability and bid request page
lineItems.description: Max with capacity, finish levels, a plans upload and an insurance-certificate request button.
Max with a testing explainer, a containment photo set and a per-room timeline.
Max when the careers page, apply form and repair form are all translated.

whatElseYouSell.name: Raking-light texture and ceiling shoot

whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, at a level-five or popcorn removal job.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile posts for drywall repairs
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Each week a patched hole or smooth ceiling goes on your Google profile with the town, so 'drywall repair near me' shows a busy shop."

whatElseYouSell.name: Review texts after homeowner drywall jobs
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "After the patch is painted, the homeowner gets a text asking for a review. Invisible drywall repairs earn the best ones."

whatElseYouSell.name: Hiring ad campaign for tapers and hangers
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A short, targeted social ad run pointing drywall finishers in {City} to your careers page, written in the trade's language."
whatElseYouSell.when: Whenever they mention being short a finisher.

whatElseYouSell.name: Builder capability sheet and truck lettering
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A one-page drywall capability sheet for builders, and lettering that makes the truck on a job site look like a company worth calling."

whatElseYouSell.name: Winter popcorn ceiling promotion
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A January push for popcorn ceiling removal fills the weeks when builders slow down for the holidays."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in November, run in January.

withoutAI.whoPays: The restoration company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Restoration crews dry out the room and cut out the wet drywall, then someone has to hang it back. They need a site, and you're who they call."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Restoration and drywall are consecutive on every water job. Warm, constant referrals.

withoutAI.route: Interior painters who need patches first
withoutAI.whoPays: The painter, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Painters find the bad drywall before they can paint. The painter you take those patches from needs a site too."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Painting and drywall share every interior job.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The GC you hang drywall for needs a project site showing finished homes, and your walls are in every photo."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Builders buy bigger sites and the sub's introduction is warm.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The yard that boom-delivers your board sells to drywall crews across the metro. A crew finder and delivery request page would be worth a lot to them."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Supply yards have budgets, and their contractor list is your next prospect list.

withoutAI.whoPays: The insulation contractor, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Insulation goes in right before you hang. The insulation crew needs a site and shares every new-build schedule with you."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Consecutive trades on the same schedule refer naturally.

withoutAI.whoPays: The testing lab or inspector, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The lab that tests popcorn ceilings before you scrape needs a simple site and booking page, and clean results lead straight to you."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Testing is the step before popcorn removal; both sides need each other.

withAI.pitchLine: "Restoration techs photograph the cut-out walls and get a draft drywall rebuild scope with sheet counts to send the sub."
withAI.whyItWorks: Restorers write rebuild scopes daily, and every one routes drywall to your client.

withAI.route: Supply yard order assistant for crews
withAI.pitchLine: "Crews text a room list and get a drafted board, mud, tape and bead order with a delivery slot from the yard."
withAI.whyItWorks: Easier ordering keeps crews loyal to one yard.

withAI.pitchLine: "When insulation inspection passes, the bot texts the drywall crew a hang date and confirms the board delivery."
withAI.whyItWorks: Builders lose days to sub coordination; drywall is the biggest gap.

withAI.pitchLine: "The painter you trade patches with loses quotes to slow follow-up. The same follow-up setup, configured for them."
withAI.whyItWorks: A second build of a working tool, introduced by a client.

withAI.pitchLine: "Homeowners ask insulation crews the same efficiency questions. A bot trained on their answers books the attic and wall jobs before drywall."
withAI.whyItWorks: Repetitive questions slow insulation sales and the bot routes work ahead of the drywall.

withAI.route: Testing lab's sample booking and results explainer
withAI.pitchLine: "Homeowners book a popcorn ceiling sample online and get a plain-language explanation of results, with next steps to a drywall pro."
withAI.whyItWorks: Labs field confused calls about results; plain summaries cut them.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back asking for a damage photo
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Mud on your hands? The caller gets a text asking for a photo of the drywall damage with a tape measure in it."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their number forwarded and two lines of wording they approve.

softwareAI.name: Applicant pipeline for hangers and tapers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every drywall applicant in one list with role, experience and a tap-to-call, instead of DMs scattered across three apps."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 1, alongside the careers page. Needs their roles and pay ranges.

softwareAI.name: Review replies for drywall and popcorn jobs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A homeowner raves about their smooth new ceiling, and a short reply that mentions the popcorn removal is drafted for your okay."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs ten past replies. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Drywall patch price guide
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Pick doorknob hole, ceiling stain or popcorn room, enter rough size, and see a range before sending the photo."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their minimum charge and prices by damage type.

softwareAI.name: Damage photo to repair estimate draft
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A homeowner's photo of a water-stained ceiling comes in and it drafts the drywall repair scope and visit count for you to check."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs past repair photos with final prices. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Invoice on completion for patch jobs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Mark the drywall patch done and the invoice with a card link goes out before you've loaded the truck."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their payment account.

softwareAI.name: Board takeoff from builder plans
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Upload a builder's floor plan and it drafts drywall sheet counts by room and ceiling height for the bid, for you to check."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, for shops bidding new construction. Needs past plans with actual board counts. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Builder job schedule with hang, tape and finish days
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every house on one drywall board: delivery, hang, tape, coats and sanding days by crew, so no builder gets a no-show."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their crews, builders and typical days per house.

softwareAI.name: After-hours water-damage intake
softwareAI.pitchLine: "At night it asks whether the leak is stopped and whether the ceiling sags, takes a photo, and books the first drywall slot."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their calendar and safety questions. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Insurance certificate and lien waiver sender
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a builder asks for a certificate or a lien waiver, it goes out from the drywall office in minutes, not days."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their document templates and insurer contact.

softwareAI.name: Crew time and sheet log
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each crew logs boards hung and hours per house on a phone, so you see who's fast and which builder jobs run long."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs crew leads willing to log daily.

softwareAI.name: Texture page writer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each month a page like 'matching knockdown after a leak', drafted from your drywall notes and approved before it goes up."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs short job notes and approval. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Chatbot on texture, dust and popcorn testing
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'will the patch show' and 'do I need to test my popcorn ceiling' at midnight, from your own drywall rules."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their FAQ and testing referral process. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Builder bid tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every drywall bid with builder, plan set, price and status in one list, with a reminder to follow up."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their current bids.

softwareAI.name: Job costing by builder and house
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See which builders' houses actually make money once board, mud, callbacks and crew hours are counted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the crew log and supply invoices for a season.

softwareAI.name: Popcorn testing and containment reminders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each popcorn ceiling booking triggers the testing referral and a prep text about clearing the room and containment day."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their testing partner process and prep checklist.

softwareAI.name: Voice notes to drywall repair quote
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Talk through the damage room by room and it drafts the drywall repair quote before you leave the driveway."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their quote template and prices. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Supply yard price sync for board and mud
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When drywall sheet and compound prices change at the yard, bids and the patch guide update the same day."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the yard's price sheet.

softwareAI.name: Applicant screener for drywall finishers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants say whether they hang, tape, run stilts or spray texture, and only real drywall finishers reach your phone."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, with the careers page. Needs must-haves and pay. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Bilingual drywall job sheet builder
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Pick the punch items from a list and the drywall job sheet prints in English and Spanish side by side, so nothing's lost on site."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their common punch items, checked once by a bilingual crew lead.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the drywall careers page for every shop
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every drywall shop is short a taper. The careers page and applicant pipeline I built for one shop fit them all."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Labour shortage is the trade's universal pain; a small monthly tool spreads fast.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Crew finder for a gypsum supply distributor
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Builders ask the gypsum yard who's available to hang. A crew finder on the distributor's site routes them to customers."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Distributors keep crews loyal by sending them work.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Wall and ceiling contractors' association member kit
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Give member drywall shops a capability page, a careers page and a repair form as a membership benefit."

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Apprenticeship and training centre recruiting site
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "The drywall training program needs a site that fills classes, and the shops that hire grads want it too."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Training programs have budgets tied to enrolment.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Agencies don't know drywall. License my template with the texture gallery, photo repair form and careers page."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies keep the client; you sell the finished drywall module.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each restoration franchise location needs vetted drywall partners for rebuilds. A partner page per location, from one template."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One contract reaches many locations with constant rebuild work.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Builders with many lots need a portal where drywall and paint subs see schedules and post completion photos."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Builders pay to cut coordination, and you already know the drywall side.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every rental turnover has wall damage. A fixed-price drywall patch request across the portfolio makes it routine."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Managers buy repeatable fixes at set prices.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Shops send in their board and compound invoices, and each month they get back where drywall material costs are heading, nothing beyond what was sent."

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Starter pack for finishers going solo
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Finishers starting their own shop, per pack
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A finisher going solo needs a patch price sheet, a capability page and a texture gallery. Sell the drywall pack your first client uses."

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Drywall shop in the next metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A drywall client in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Drywall crews don't compete across metros. The careers-first template that filled one shop's crew goes to the next city."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse everything.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The drywall shop with a dead site
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Drywall sites with stale hiring posts and broken forms are common. I move them to a working template quickly."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Cheap, fast and easy to say yes to.
